content: Certainly. 1. Administer 375 mg of hyoscyamine orally every 12 hours. Avoid long-term use due to a high incidence of anticholinergic side effects, as noted in the Beers criteria. Glucagon increases the toxicity of hyoscyamine through additive effects on gastrointestinal motility inhibition. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 2. Co-administration of anticholinergic drugs and glucagon increases the risk of gastrointestinal adverse reactions due to additive effects on the inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Intranasal glucagon increases the toxicity of hyoscyamine through additive effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Topical glycopyrronium tosylate and hyoscyamine may increase each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with other anticholinergic medications may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. 5. Pramlintide and hyoscyamine increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to synergistic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. 6. Revefenacin and hyoscyamine both decrease cholinergic effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as co-administration may cause additive anticholinergic effects. 7. Hyoscyamine decreases the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Concomitant use of anticholinergic drugs may cause a hyporesponse to secretin stimulation testing. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 8. Topical sofpironium and hyoscyamine increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as additive anticholinergic adverse effects may occur. 9. Hyoscyamine and inhaled umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as concomitant use with other anticholinergic-containing drugs may lead to additive anticholinergic adverse effects. 10. Hyoscyamine increases the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor, as drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 11. Hyoscyamine and aclidinium both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 12. Hyoscyamine and amantadine may increase anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Hyoscyamine and amitriptyline both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 14. Hyoscyamine and amoxapine both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 15. Anticholinergic/sedative combinations and hyoscyamine both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 16. Hyoscyamine decreases the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Hyoscyamine also decreases aripiprazole levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while aripiprazole increases the effects of hyoscyamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia. 17. Atracurium and hyoscyamine both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. 18. Use caution and monitor, as additive anticholinergic adverse effects may occur with concurrent use. 24. Bethanechol increases cholinergic effects, while hyoscyamine decreases them. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution and monitor. 25. Long-acting injectable buprenorphine increases the effects of hyoscyamine through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor, as co-administration may increase the risk of urinary retention and/or severe constipation, potentially leading to paralytic ileus. 26.
